name: Pancreas
description: A dual-purpose gland that releases digestive enzymes into the gut and the hormones that steady blood sugar.

keyFacts.label: Daily
keyFacts.value: Makes about 1.5 L of enzyme-rich juice

keyFacts.label: Location
keyFacts.value: Behind the stomach, across the upper abdomen

medicalImportance: Islets of Langerhans release insulin and glucagon to balance blood sugar.
didYouKnow: Barely 2% of it makes hormones; the rest is given over to digestive enzymes.

parts.name: Head of Pancreas & Uncinate
parts.description: The expanded, disc-shaped rightmost portion nestled within the concavity of the C-shaped duodenal loop at L2 vertebra, featuring the hook-like Uncinate Process projecting posteroinferiorly behind the superior mesenteric vessels.
parts.function: Major exocrine digestive factory producing over 1 liter/day of alkaline pancreatic juice containing trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, pancreatic lipase, and amylase for macronutrient breakdown.
connections: Intimately embraced by 1st, 2nd, and 3rd parts of Duodenum
Traversed posteriorly by the terminal Common Bile Duct as it heads to the Ampulla of Vater
Uncinate process crossed anteriorly by Superior Mesenteric Artery and Vein
Empties exocrine juice via Main Duct of Wirsung and Accessory Duct of Santorini
parts.clinicalNote: Pancreatic head adenocarcinoma (~70% of all pancreatic malignancies) compresses the distal common bile duct early, causing painless obstructive jaundice with pruritus, pale acholic stools, dark tea urine, and palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier sign).
keyFeatures: Nestled in duodenal C-loop; sharing pancreaticoduodenal arterial arcade vascularization
Uncinate process hook wraps behind the Superior Mesenteric Artery / Vein
Surgically resected via the Whipple procedure (pancreaticoduodenectomy)
Acinar cells package digestive pro-enzymes into protective zymogen granules
parts.histology: Densely packed serous acini with apical zymogen granules surrounding narrow central intercalated ducts lined with centroacinar cells that secrete bicarbonate under Secretin stimulus.

parts.name: Body & Tail of Pancreas
parts.description: The elongated prism-shaped body crossing horizontally to the left over the aorta and left renal vessels, tapering into the narrow mobile tail which enters the splenorenal ligament to contact the splenic hilum.
parts.function: Concentrated endocrine powerhouse containing dense clusters of Islets of Langerhans that directly regulate glucose metabolism via insulin and glucagon secretion.
connections: Posterior surface grooved by the tortuous Splenic Artery and straight Splenic Vein
Rests anterior to Left Kidney, Left Suprarenal Gland, and Renal Hilum
Anterior surface covered by peritoneum forming the posterior wall of the lesser sac
Tail tip terminates within Splenorenal Ligament touching the visceral surface of Spleen
parts.clinicalNote: During splenectomy, accidental ligation or crushing of the pancreatic tail in the splenic hilum leads to pancreatic fistula or postoperative pseudocyst formation. Acute pancreatitis (gallstones or alcohol) releases activated elastase causing retroperitoneal auto-digestion and Grey Turner / Cullen signs.
keyFeatures: Highest density of endocrine Islets of Langerhans (~1 million islets total in gland)
Beta cells (~70% of islet mass) secrete Insulin in response to elevated blood glucose
Alpha cells (~20%) secrete Glucagon; Delta cells (~5%) secrete Somatostatin
Tail is the only intraperitoneal mobile portion of the otherwise retroperitoneal gland
parts.histology: Vascularized spherical Islets of Langerhans embedded like cellular islands within exocrine acinar parenchyma, enveloped by fenestrated capillaries allowing rapid hormone release into portal circulation.

quizBank.prompt: What proportion of pancreatic parenchyma performs endocrine vs exocrine functions?
quizBank.rationale: Islets of Langerhans occupy only about 1 to 2% of total pancreatic mass; the vast majority produces digestive pancreatic juice.
